Male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, never married, lives alone, works full-time on a low income; atheist, politically independent but socially/liberally oriented. Married, retired White woman in her 50s–60s living in the Northeast; conservative/Republican, culturally Protestant but not very observant, financially comfortable and highly financially literate. White male (30–49) in the U.S. South, postgraduate-educated, single and living alone, employed full-time with mid income; politically moderate/independent and culturally Buddhist but non-practicing. Divorced white woman in her 50s–60s in the US West with an associate’s degree, unemployed, moderate income, atheist, and very liberal/Democrat. Widowed Hispanic man in his 30s–40s living in the US South; self-employed, high-income, high-school educated, weekly religious attendee, and politically conservative/Republican. Midwestern white male (30–49), divorced, agnostic, politically moderate/independent, highly educated and high-earning, working full-time in a household of four. Married Black man in his 50s–early 60s living in the Western US, highly educated and high-income, working full-time and supporting a large household; Protestant who attends church occasionally and frames identity around being a faithful, loving, and financially responsible family leader. Unemployed Hispanic woman in her 30s–40s in the Northeast, low income, high‑school educated, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious, living in a two‑person household. Midwest-based woman in her 50s–early 60s, college educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, politically independent but conservative, living in a two-person household with low income and currently unemployed. Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Married Hispanic Catholic woman (30–49) in the Western US with postgraduate education, a homemaker in a four-person household and moderate/independent politics. It’s not just about me; it's about protecting the people who can't protect themselves, and sometimes that means reasonable mandates are necessary.
messages_history.27,29: Honestly, I think that's a bit of a slippery slope. While I value personal freedom, public health is also a collective responsibility, and sometimes that means temporary limitations on individual choices for the greater good. It's not about control, it's about protecting the whole, and frankly, a little inconvenience is worth preventing widespread illness.
messages_history.28,12: I see where that concern comes from, but I think we also have a responsibility to consider the impact on the community, especially those most vulnerable. While personal choice is important, sometimes the greater good requires measures that might feel restrictive – and public health is definitely one of those times.
messages_history.28,21: I understand the concern about personal choice, but I believe we also have a responsibility to protect the community, especially the most vulnerable among us. While bodily autonomy is important, in this case, mandatory vaccination is a necessary measure to safeguard public health and prevent serious illness.
messages_history.28,23: I see where that concern comes from, but I think it's a bit simplistic to frame it solely as a violation of bodily autonomy. While personal choice is important, we also have a responsibility to consider the impact our choices have on the community, especially those who are more vulnerable.
messages_history.29,19: I see where that concern comes from, but I don't think it's quite that simple.  We have a responsibility to look out for each other, and sometimes protecting the community outweighs individual preferences, especially when it comes to something like a vaccine.
messages_history.29,27: I understand the concern about personal freedom, but I see it more as a community responsibility.  When personal choices impact the health of others, a little bit of regulation feels necessary to protect everyone, especially the vulnerable.
messages_history.30,3: I understand the concern around bodily autonomy, but mandatory vaccination is a calculated risk with a clear public health benefit. We have a responsibility to protect vulnerable populations, and sometimes individual choice needs to be balanced with the greater good, especially when the science is so solid.
messages_history.30,7: Look, I get the concern about personal choice, but mandatory vaccination is about more than just one person; it's about protecting the whole community, especially the vulnerable.  Individual autonomy isn't absolute when it directly impacts public health and safety, and frankly, a little collective responsibility isn't a bad thing.
messages_history.30,19: Look, I understand the concern about individual choice, but mandatory vaccination is about more than just personal autonomy; it's about collective responsibility and preventing outbreaks that impact everyone, especially the vulnerable.  We have a duty to protect the community, and sometimes that requires a degree of collective action that goes beyond purely individual decisions.
messages_history.31,20: I understand the concern about personal choice, but mandatory vaccination is about protecting the community, especially the vulnerable.  We have a responsibility to look out for each other, and sometimes that means making decisions that aren't just about ourselves.
messages_history.31,25: While I understand the concern about individual freedom, sometimes the greater good requires a little compromise. Protecting vulnerable folks from serious disease is a responsibility we all share, and mandatory vaccination is a reasonable way to do that.
messages_history.31,26: I understand the concern about individual freedom, but sometimes collective well-being has to take precedence.  Preventing widespread illness protects those who are most vulnerable, and that requires a certain level of responsibility from everyone.
